Maya.why: She took the belly on to the tail without being asked, closed the joint gap, and gave a clear, accurate public status at the end, which is strong impact and execution. She said she would inspect the finished chain and didn't, and her leadership was more speaking for the team than directing it, so she falls just short of the top spot.

Tom.why: He laid the belly start, fixed a kink, and carefully cleared the pale strays after checking with Leo, with good collaboration and discipline about staying hands-off. His belly was the slowest piece, Maya had to finish it, and how much he laid is unverified, so his impact is medium.

Priya.why: She laid the lower tail fork and gave accurate summaries and generous credit, so she was a reliable teammate, but her laid contribution was modest and Leo had to cover the top prong. She duplicated Maya's gap work, said the tail was 'hers' before placing anything, and was passive after about four minutes. The gap to Tom is small, and the forced curve puts her at the bottom.

Leo.why: He chose the fish, sketched the plan, assigned strokes, laid the start line, nose and top tail prong, and reassigned work when the belly lagged. Teammates consistently credit him, and his instruction to lift only the pale pieces kept the dark line safe, though he is somewhat bossy and was silent at the end.
